title: Organization of laboratory services. Medical ethics and deontology

slides.title: Organization of laboratory services. Medical ethics and deontology
bullets: Practical class (4 hours) + values and ethics class (2 hours)

slides.title: Aims and plan of the class
bullets: Laboratory service — tasks, structure, the specimen pathway
Quality system — the 12 elements of WHO LQMS, ISO 15189
Safety — general, fire, biological; hand hygiene and PPE
Medical ethics and deontology — principles, confidentiality, honesty
Values and ethics class — professional duty, teamwork, responsibility to the patient
Wrap-up — case scenarios, mini-test and oral questions
slides.note: By the end of the class students should be able to name the phases of the testing process, the elements of the quality system, the main safety rules and the principles of ethics.

slides.title: Organization of laboratory services
bullets: The laboratory is an integral part of the diagnostic process

slides.title: Tasks of the clinical laboratory
bullets: Diagnosis — A reliable result to detect and confirm disease
Monitoring — Following treatment effectiveness and the course of disease
Screening — Early detection of hidden disease, assessment of risk factors
Emergency care — Timely communication of critical results to the physician
Quality and safety — Accurate results, staff and patient safety
Education and research — Training staff, introducing new methods
slides.note: Laboratory results underpin many clinical decisions — so the cost of an error is high. Example: if a potassium result is wrong (haemolysis), the wrong treatment may be started.

slides.title: The laboratory team: who does what
bullets: Head of laboratory — Responsible for organizing the work, the quality system and safety
Clinical laboratory physician — Clinical review and validation of results, consultation with physicians
Laboratory technician — Specimen reception, performing tests, QC, equipment care
Support staff — Cleaning, disinfection, orderly waste collection
slides.note: General roles. Exact staff positions and job descriptions follow the institution and current regulations: the teacher should use the structure of their own institution as an example.

slides.title: The testing process: three phases
bullets: 1. Pre-analytical — Test request, patient preparation, specimen collection, labelling, transport, reception
2. Analytical — Measurement, calibration, internal quality control (QC), equipment maintenance
3. Post-analytical — Result review and validation, reporting, notification of critical values
slides.note: The literature shows that the largest share of laboratory errors occurs in the pre-analytical phase (about 60–70 %; Plebani M., Clin Chem Lab Med 2006). In the app: Lab → Pre-analytics (order of draw, WHO).
slides.source: Most errors arise in the pre-analytical phase (Plebani, 2006).

slides.title: The specimen pathway: from request to result
bullets: 1. Request — Physician referral, type of test
2. Identification — At least 2 identifiers: full name, date of birth or ID
3. Collection — Correct tube and order
4. Labelling — At the patient’s side, immediately
5. Transport — Time and temperature conditions
6. Reception — Checking, registration
7. Analysis — With QC
8. Report — Validation, critical value
slides.note: An error can happen at every step. Ask students to name one possible error for each step (for example: wrong patient, wrong tube, long transport, unlabelled specimen).
slides.source: The most dangerous error is the wrong patient: always identify with at least 2 identifiers.

slides.title: Specimen labelling and reception
bullets: Labelling — at least 2 identifiers, date and time of collection, the collecting staff member
When — the tube is labelled at the patient’s side, immediately after collection
Rejection — unlabelled or wrongly labelled specimen
Rejection — wrong tube, insufficient volume, clotted (in an anticoagulant tube)
Rejection — transport conditions breached (time, temperature); haemolysis — depending on the test
Recording — every rejection is recorded as an incident and the ward is notified
slides.note: Rejection criteria must be in the laboratory’s written procedure (SOP). Discussion: “An unlabelled tube arrived, but the nurse knows whose it is” — is it accepted? (No.)

slides.title: Quality system — the 12 elements of WHO LQMS
bullets: Organization — Structure, management
Personnel — Qualification, training
Equipment — Calibration, maintenance
Purchasing and inventory — Reagents, expiry
Process control — QC, specimen
Information — Results, confidentiality
Documents — SOPs, logs
Occurrences — Recording errors
Assessment — Audit, EQA
Improvement — Corrective actions
Customer service — Physician and patient feedback
Facilities and safety — Layout, protection
slides.note: Source: WHO. Laboratory Quality Management System: Handbook. 2011. International standard: ISO 15189:2022 — quality and competence of medical laboratories.

slides.title: Documents and records
bullets: SOP — for every test and process: written, approved, available at the workstation
Logs — QC results, equipment maintenance, temperature, reagent lots
Traceability — answers “who, when, with which instrument and reagent”
Occurrences — errors and nonconformities are not hidden; they are recorded and analysed
Rule — “Not written down — not done”
slides.note: Practical task: the group drafts the structure of an SOP for one simple test (for example, glucose): purpose, specimen, reagent, instrument, QC, calculation, reference interval, safety.

slides.title: Laboratory safety
bullets: Protecting staff, patients and the environment

slides.title: The general safety system
bullets: Organizational — Written safety plan and SOPs, a responsible person, training at the start of work and periodically, emergency drills
Electrical — A damaged socket/instrument is labelled and taken out of service; plugging in with wet hands is prohibited; disconnect from power for repairs
Fire — Flammable solvents in minimal amounts, in a dedicated cabinet; open flames are never left unattended; corridors kept clear
slides.note: Based on the outline of qualification-exam oral question kdl-o-006. Every staff member must know where the emergency equipment is: fire extinguisher, alarm, exit routes, emergency shower/eyewash, first-aid kit.

slides.title: In case of fire: RACE and PASS
bullets: RACE — actions — Rescue — get people out; Alarm — raise the alarm; Confine — close the door to contain; Evacuate/Extinguish — leave or put it out
PASS — extinguisher — Pull — pull the pin; Aim — at the base of the fire; Squeeze — squeeze the lever; Sweep — sweep side to side
Extinguisher class — A — ordinary combustibles; B — flammable liquids/gases; C — energized equipment; If clothing catches fire — “stop, drop and roll”
slides.note: kdl-o-006. Practical exercise: students point out the fire extinguisher, emergency shower and exit route in the laboratory.

slides.title: Biosafety: the basics
bullets: Basis — a risk assessment for every task: information → assessment → control → measures → review
BSL levels — work with blood, body fluids and tissues is usually done under BSL-2 conditions
Every specimen is treated as potentially infectious (standard precautions)
slides.note: kdl-o-007; source: WHO Laboratory Biosafety Manual, 4th ed. (2020). BSL-1 — agents that do not cause disease in healthy adults; BSL-2 — HBV, HIV, Salmonella, etc.; BSL-3/4 — serious agents transmitted by the airborne route.
slides.source: Source: WHO Laboratory Biosafety Manual, 4th edition (2020)

slides.title: Prohibited in the laboratory
bullets: Food and drink — Eating, drinking or storing food in the work area
Smoking — Smoking and applying cosmetics
Mouth pipetting — Mechanical pipettes only
“Clean” surfaces with gloves — Touching doors, phones or keyboards with gloves on
Lab coat outside — Lab coats and gloves are not worn outside the laboratory
Working unprotected — Working without eye and face protection when there is a splash risk
slides.note: kdl-o-007 outline; WHO Laboratory Biosafety Manual (2020) — good microbiological practice. Students find the warning signs in the laboratory and explain what they mean.

slides.title: Hand hygiene
bullets: Alcohol-based hand rub — 20–30 seconds, until hands are dry
Soap and water — 40–60 seconds; when hands are visibly soiled
When — at the start of work and when leaving the laboratory
When — before putting on and after removing gloves
When — after handling biological material, before eating
Remember — gloves do not replace hand hygiene
slides.note: Source: WHO Guidelines on Hand Hygiene in Health Care (2009). Practical exercise: students demonstrate the hand-rub technique (palms, between the fingers, thumbs, fingertips, wrists).
slides.source: Source: WHO Guidelines on Hand Hygiene in Health Care (2009)

slides.title: Personal protective equipment: putting on and removing
bullets: Putting on: Hand hygiene → Gown → Mask → Goggles / face shield → Gloves
Removing: Gloves → Goggles / face shield → Gown → Mask → Hand hygiene
slides.note: Source: CDC — Sequence for putting on / removing PPE. When removing, the most contaminated item (gloves) comes off first; do not touch the outer surface.
slides.source: Source: CDC, Sequence for putting on and removing PPE. Removal — starting with the most contaminated.

slides.title: Biosafety: practice
bullets: Sharps — needles are never recapped; straight into a puncture-resistant container
Aerosols — centrifuge and open tubes in sealed buckets or in a biological safety cabinet
Spills — follow a ready procedure: contain, disinfect, clean up
Work surfaces — disinfect at the end of work and after every spill
slides.note: kdl-o-007. Decontamination: infectious material is decontaminated before disposal (preferably by autoclaving).
slides.source: Source: WHO Laboratory Biosafety Manual, 4th edition (2020)

slides.title: Needlestick injury or blood on a mucous membrane
bullets: 1. Immediately — Skin — wash with running water and soap; eyes/mucosa — rinse with plenty of water
2. Report — Inform the supervisor immediately, record the incident
3. Prophylaxis — Post-exposure assessment and prophylaxis according to the institution’s procedure — as soon as possible
slides.note: kdl-o-007: staff health — occupational health requirements (including vaccination), the post-exposure prophylaxis procedure. Specific drugs and time limits follow the institution’s protocol and current national guidance — the teacher should explain the local procedure.
slides.source: Every laboratory must have a written post-exposure procedure known to all staff.

slides.title: Medical waste
bullets: Sharps — Needles, lancets, glass — puncture-resistant container; closed when ¾ full
Infectious — Bag/container with the biohazard symbol; decontaminate before disposal (autoclave)
Chemical — Reagent residues — separately, according to the label and safety data sheet
National requirements — Waste classes, colours and procedures — per the current sanitary rules
slides.note: Source: WHO, Safe management of wastes from health-care activities (2014). Waste classes and colours are set by the country’s sanitary rules — the teacher should state the current national procedure.
slides.source: Source: WHO, Safe management of wastes from health-care activities (2014)

slides.title: Medical ethics and deontology
bullets: Professional duty and conduct

slides.title: Concepts and core principles
bullets: Medical ethics — Moral principles in relation to patients, colleagues and society
Deontology — The study of professional duty and rules of conduct
Patient’s interest — Putting the patient’s interest first, doing no harm
Autonomy — Patient rights and voluntary informed consent
Non-discrimination — Care based only on medical need
Justice — The same quality and attention for every patient
slides.note: Based on the kdl-o-037 outline.

slides.title: Confidentiality in the laboratory
bullets: Medical secrecy — results and patient data only for authorized persons
Without time limit — the obligation continues even after the patient’s death
Telephone — results are not given to outsiders by phone
Forms — not left in the open; screens are locked
Electronic system — personal login; passwords are never shared
Social media — no posting of results or specimen photos
slides.note: Discussion: “My neighbour asked for her friend’s test result” — how does the laboratory technician answer?

slides.title: Professional honesty and accountability
bullets: Competence — Continuous learning and professional development; do not perform an unfamiliar method on your own
Honesty — Errors are not hidden — they are recorded and corrected. “Adjusting” a result is prohibited
Critical result — A life-threatening value is reported to the physician immediately and recorded
Colleagues — Respect and clear communication; a colleague is not criticized in front of a patient
slides.note: kdl-o-037. In Uzbekistan the code of ethics for medical workers was approved by Ministry of Health order No. 88 of 24 March 2022 — the teacher should check the text on lex.uz and read out its main requirements.
slides.source: Code of ethics for medical workers (Ministry of Health, 2022, order No. 88) — check the text on lex.uz

slides.title: Values and ethics class
bullets: A profession is a responsibility

slides.title: The laboratory technician — unseen, but decisive
bullets: Behind every tube is a person: a child, a mother, an elderly patient
Accuracy is care: a correctly labelled specimen saves lives
Teamwork — trust between the laboratory, the clinic and the patient
Never stop learning — medicine changes every year
Honesty — saying “I don’t know, I will find out” is professional courage
slides.note: The teacher is encouraged to share one story from their own experience. Discussion: “Why did I choose this profession?”

slides.title: Practical scenarios (discussion)
bullets: 1 — A specimen arrived unlabelled. What do you do?
2 — Potassium 7.2 mmol/L, the specimen is haemolysed. Do you release the result?
3 — A colleague wants to send results even though QC is “out”.
4 — You got a needlestick injury. Your first 3 actions?
5 — A patient’s relative asked for the result by phone.
slides.note: Expected answers: 1) not accepted, recollection is requested, the incident is recorded; 2) haemolysis falsely raises potassium — report with a comment or recollect the specimen, inform the physician; 3) patient results are not released until QC meets the requirements — the cause is found and fixed; 4) wash, inform the supervisor, follow the post-exposure procedure; 5) results are not given to an unauthorized person.

slides.title: Mini-test
bullets: 1. In which phase do most laboratory errors occur?
2. At which biosafety level is work with blood usually done?
3. What is removed first when taking off PPE?
4. How long does hand rubbing with an alcohol-based antiseptic take?
slides.note: Answers: 1 — A (pre-analytical); 2 — B (BSL-2); 3 — C (gloves); 4 — B (20–30 seconds). Group test in the app: Learn → Groups → topic → test.
